plan: 2 Samuel 8:15-18; 1 Chronicles 18:14-17; 1 Chronicles 6:16-30, 50-53, 31-48; 2 Samuel 9:1-13; 2 Samuel 10:1-19; 1 Chronicles 19:1-19

readings.title: Dawid's Righteous Reign
readings.text: [2 Samuel 8:15] So Dawiḏ reigned over all Yisra’ĕl. And Dawiḏ was doing right-ruling and righteousness to all his people. [16] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah was over the army, and Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder; [17] and Tsaḏoq son of Aḥituḇ and Aḥimelek son of Eḇyathar were the priests, and Serayah was the scribe; [18] and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa was over both the Kerethites and Pelĕthites. And the sons of Dawiḏ were priests.

readings.title: Officials of the Kingdom
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 18:14] So Dawiḏ reigned over all Yisra’ĕl, and he was doing right-ruling and righteousness to all his people. [15] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah was over the army, and Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder; [16] and Tsaḏoq son of Aḥituḇ, and Aḇimelek son of Eḇyathar were the priests, and Shawsha was the scribe; [17] and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa was over the Kerethites and the Pelĕthites. And the sons of Dawiḏ were chiefs at the king’s side.

readings.title: Descendants of Lĕwi
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 6:16] The sons of Lĕwi: Gĕrshom, Qehath, and Merari. [17] And these are the names of the sons of Gĕrshom: Liḇni and Shim‛i. [18] And the sons of Qehath: Amram, and Yitshar, and Ḥeḇron, and Uzzi’ĕl. [19] The sons of Merari: Maḥli and Mushi. And these are the clans of the Lĕwites according to their fathers: [20] Of Gĕrshom: Liḇni his son, Yaḥath his son, Zimmah his son, [21] Yo’aḥ his son, Iddo his son, Zeraḥ his son, Ye’atherai his son. [22] The sons of Qehath: Amminaḏaḇ his son, Qoraḥ his son, Assir his son, [23] Elqanah his son, and Eḇyasaph his son, and Assir his son, [24] Taḥath his son, Uri’ĕl his son, Uzziyah his son, and Sha’ul his son. [25] And the sons of Elqanah: Amasai and Aḥimoth. [26] As for Elqanah, the sons of Elqanah: Tsophai his son, and Naḥath his son, [27] Eliyaḇ his son, Yeroḥam his son, Elqanah his son. [28] And the sons of Shemu’ĕl: the first-born Washni, and Aḇiyah. [29] The sons of Merari: Maḥli, Liḇni his son, Shim‛i his son, Uzzah his son, [30] Shim‛a his son, Ḥaggiyah his son, Asayah his son.

readings.title: Descendants of Aharon
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 6:50] And these are the sons of Aharon: El‛azar his son, Pinḥas his son, Aḇishu‛a his son, [51] Buqqi his son, Uzzi his son, Zeraḥyah his son, [52] Merayoth his son, Amaryah his son, Aḥituḇ his son, [53] Tsaḏoq his son, Aḥima‛ats his son.

readings.title: The Musicians of the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 6:31] And these are the men whom Dawiḏ appointed over the service of song in the house of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, after the ark came to rest. [32] And they were ministering with song before the Dwelling Place of the Tent of Meeting, until Shelomoh had built the house of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Yerushalayim, and they served in their office according to their order. [33] And these are the ones who stood with their sons: Of the sons of the Qehathites: Hĕman the singer, son of Yo’ĕl, son of Shemu’ĕl, [34] son of Elqanah, son of Yeroḥam, son of Eli’ĕl, son of Toaḥ, [35] son of Tsuph, son of Elqanah, son of Maḥath, son of Amasai, [36] son of Elqanah, son of Yo’ĕl, son of Azaryah, son of Tsephanyah, [37] son of Taḥath, son of Assir, son of Eḇyasaph, son of Qoraḥ, [38] son of Yitshar, son of Qehath, son of Lĕwi, son of Yisra’ĕl. [39] And his brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand: Asaph son of Bereḵyah, son of Shim‛a, [40] son of Miḵa’ĕl, son of Ba‛aseyah, son of Malkiyah, [41] son of Ethni, son of Zeraḥ, son of Aḏayah, [42] son of Ěythan, son of Zimmah, son of Shim‛i, [43] son of Yaḥath, son of Gĕrshom, son of Lĕwi. [44] And their brothers, the sons of Merari, on the left hand: Ěythan son of Qishi, son of Aḇḏi, son of Malluḵ, [45] son of Ḥashaḇyah, son of Amatsyah, son of Ḥilqiyah, [46] son of Amtsi, son of Bani, son of Shemer, [47] son of Maḥli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Lĕwi. [48] And their brothers the Lĕwites were appointed to all the service of the Dwelling Place of the house of <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: Dawid and Mepiḇosheth
readings.text: [2 Samuel 9:1] And Dawiḏ said, “Is there still anyone who is left of the house of Sha’ul, that I might show him kindness for Yonathan’s sake?” [2] And there was a servant of the house of Sha’ul whose name was Tsiḇa. So when they had called him to Dawiḏ, the king said to him, “Are you Tsiḇa?” And he said, “Your servant.” [3] And the king said, “Is there not still someone of the house of Sha’ul, to whom I might show the kindness of <dn>Elohim</dn>?” And Tsiḇa said to the king, “There is still a son of Yonathan who is lame in his feet.” [4] And the king said to him, “Where is he?” And Tsiḇa said to the king, “See, he is in the house of Maḵir son of Ammi’ĕl, in Lo Deḇar.” [5] And Sovereign Dawiḏ sent and brought him out of the house of Maḵir son of Ammi’ĕl, from Lo Deḇar. [6] And when Mepiḇosheth son of Yonathan, son of Sha’ul, came to Dawiḏ, he fell on his face and did obeisance. And Dawiḏ said, “Mepiḇosheth?” And he answered, “Here is your servant!” [7] And Dawiḏ said to him, “Do not fear, for I shall certainly show you kindness for Yonathan your father’s sake, and shall return to you <dn>את</dn> all the land of Sha’ul your grandfather. And you shall eat bread at my table continually.” [8] And he bowed himself, and said, “What is your servant, that you should look upon such a dead dog as I?” [9] And the king called to Tsiḇa, Sha’ul’s servant, and said to him, “All that belonged to Sha’ul and to all his house I have given to your master’s son. [10] “And you shall till <dn>את</dn> the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and you shall bring in the harvest, and it shall be food for your master’s son to eat. But Mepiḇosheth your master’s son shall eat bread at my table continually.” Now Tsiḇa had fifteen sons and twenty servants. [11] And Tsiḇa said to the king, “According to all that my master the king has commanded his servant, so your servant does.” “As for Mepiḇosheth,” said the king, “he shall eat at my table like one of the king’s sons.” [12] And Mepiḇosheth had a young son whose name was Miḵa. And all who dwelt in the house of Tsiḇa were servants to Mepiḇosheth. [13] So Mepiḇosheth dwelt in Yerushalayim, for he ate continually at the king’s table. And he was lame in both his feet.

readings.title: The Defeat of Ammon and Aram
readings.text: [2 Samuel 10:1] And it came to be after this that the sovereign of the children of Ammon died, and Ḥanun his son reigned in his place. [2] And Dawiḏ said, “I am going to show kindness to Ḥanun son of Naḥash, as his father showed kindness to me.” So Dawiḏ sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And Dawiḏ’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon. [3] And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Ḥanun their master, “Do you think Dawiḏ is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Has Dawiḏ not rather sent his servants to you to search <dn>את</dn> the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?” [4] Therefore Ḥanun took <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ’s servants, and shaved off <dn>את</dn> half of their beards, and cut off <dn>את</dn> their garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away. [5] And they informed Dawiḏ, and he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, “Wait at Yereḥo until your beards have grown, and then return.” [6] And the children of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to Dawiḏ, so the children of Ammon sent and hired <dn>את</dn> the Arameans of Bĕyth Reḥoḇ and <dn>את</dn> the Arameans of Tsoḇa, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ma‛aḵah, one thousand men, and <dn>את</dn> Ish-Toḇ, twelve thousand men. [7] And Dawiḏ heard of it, and he sent <dn>את</dn> Yo’aḇ and <dn>את</dn> all the army of the mighty men. [8] And the children of Ammon came out and put themselves in battle array at the entrance of the gate. And the Arameans of Tsoḇa, and Reḥoḇ, and Ish-Toḇ, and Ma‛aḵah, were by themselves in the field. [9] And Yo’aḇ saw that the battle line was against him before and behind, so he chose of all the choice men of Yisra’ĕl and put them in battle array against the Arameans. [10] And <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people he gave under the hand of Aḇishai his brother, and put them in battle array against the children of Ammon. [11] And he said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I shall come and help you. [12] “Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do what is good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.” [13] And Yo’aḇ and the people who were with him drew near for the battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him. [14] And when the children of Ammon saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they also fled before Aḇishai, and entered the city. And Yo’aḇ returned from the children of Ammon and went to Yerushalayim. [15] And when the Arameans saw that they were smitten before Yisra’ĕl, they gathered together. [16] And Haḏaḏ‛ezer sent and brought out <dn>את</dn> the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Hĕylam. And Shoḇaḵ the commander of Haḏaḏ‛ezer’s army went before them. [17] And it was reported to Dawiḏ, and he gathered <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl, and passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn, and came to Hĕylam. And the Arameans set themselves in battle array against Dawiḏ, and fought with him. [18] And Aram fled before Yisra’ĕl, and Dawiḏ killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen of the Arameans, and smote <dn>את</dn> Shoḇaḵ the commander of their army, who died there. [19] And when all the sovereigns, the servants of Haḏaḏ‛ezer, saw that they were smitten by Yisra’ĕl, they made peace with Yisra’ĕl and served them. And the Arameans were afraid to help the children of Ammon anymore.

readings.title: The Ammonite and Aramean Coalition Falls
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 19:1] And it came to be after this that Naḥash sovereign of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place. [2] And Dawiḏ said, “I am going to show kindness to Ḥanun son of Naḥash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So Dawiḏ sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And Dawiḏ’s servants came to Ḥanun in the land of the children of Ammon to comfort him. [3] And the princes of the children of Ammon said to Ḥanun, “Do you think Dawiḏ is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Have his servants not come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?” [4] Therefore Ḥanun took <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ’s servants and shaved them, and cut off <dn>את</dn> their garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away. [5] And some went and informed Dawiḏ about the men, and he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, “Wait at Yereḥo until your beards have grown, and then return.” [6] And the children of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to Dawiḏ, so Ḥanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Aram Naharayim, and from Aram Ma‛aḵah, and from Tsoḇah. [7] And they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the sovereign of Ma‛aḵah and his people, who came and encamped before Mĕḏeḇa. And the children of Ammon gathered together from their cities, and came to battle. [8] And Dawiḏ heard of it, and he sent Yo’aḇ and all the army of the mighty men. [9] And the children of Ammon came out and put themselves in battle array before the gate of the city, and the sovereigns who had come were by themselves in the field. [10] And Yo’aḇ saw that the battle line was against him before and behind, so he chose of all the choice men of Yisra’ĕl, and put them in battle array against the Arameans. [11] And <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people he gave under the hand of Aḇishai his brother, and they put themselves in battle array against the children of Ammon. [12] And he said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I shall help you. [13] “Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do what is good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.” [14] And Yo’aḇ and the people who were with him drew near for the battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him. [15] And when the children of Ammon saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they also fled before Aḇishai his brother, and entered the city. And Yo’aḇ went to Yerushalayim. [16] And when the Arameans saw that they had been smitten by Yisra’ĕl, they sent messengers and brought <dn>את</dn> the Arameans who were beyond the River, and Shophaḵ the commander of Haḏaḏ‛ezer’s army went before them. [17] And it was reported to Dawiḏ, and he gathered <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl, and passed over the Yardĕn, and came upon them, and set up in battle array against them. And when Dawiḏ had set up in battle array against the Arameans, they fought with him. [18] And Aram fled before Yisra’ĕl, and Dawiḏ killed seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers of the Arameans, and killed <dn>את</dn> Shophaḵ commander of the army. [19] And when the servants of Haḏaḏ‛ezer saw that they had been smitten by Yisra’ĕl, they made peace with Dawiḏ and served him. And Aram would not help the children of Ammon anymore.
